stories.title: Avengers Infinity Gauntlet Medal Recall — Dangerous Magnets

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: ⚠️ Recall: The Conqueror's Avengers Infinity Gauntlet medal recalled — magnets can detach, child ingestion risk. ~476 units sold ~$50 on their app, Mar–May 2026. Refund/replace: theconqueror.events/recall-inf #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting
x_posts.tweet_type: National Parenting — Product Safety / CPSC Recall

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Have the Avengers Infinity Gauntlet medal from The Conqueror's virtual race app? It's recalled — magnets can detach. Call 833-799-0368 or visit theconqueror.events/recall-inf for a refund/replacement. Keep it from kids. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting
x_posts.tweet_type: National Parenting — Product Safety / CPSC Recall

facebook.long_form:
If your kid is into virtual racing challenges, heads up on a recall you'll want to know about.

The Conqueror recalled approximately 476 Avengers Infinity Gauntlet licensed medals on October 8th. The medals contain high-powered magnets that can detach from the product — and magnet ingestion is one of the more serious child safety hazards out there. When two or more magnets are swallowed, they can attract through intestinal walls and cause tears, blockages, or worse. The CPSC noted three reports of magnets detaching, and no injuries so far.

The medal is gold-colored with colorful gems, sold in a black package marked "Marvel Avengers." It was available through The Conqueror's website and app from March through May 2026 for around $50.

If you have one: stop using it and keep it away from kids. You can get a full refund or a replacement medal by contacting The Conqueror at 833-799-0368 (Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM ET) or through the recall page at theconqueror.events/recall-inf.

facebook.long_form:
D49 families, we're officially at T-minus one day. 🎉

Fall break starts Monday, October 12th, and runs through October 19th (back on the 20th). That's eight school days to fill with something better than uninterrupted screen time — no judgment, but here's what's actually happening around Colorado Springs this week.

**Free (or mostly free) options:**
Cool Science Festival runs through October 18th at multiple venues around COS. Garden of the Gods is free to access all year, and mid-October is genuinely one of the best times for the trails — fall color peaks this week.

**Tickets required:**
Boo at the Zoo at Cheyenne Mountain Zoo runs all October weekends. It's worth the price and often sells out, so get tickets early if you haven't already.

**For the outdoorsy crowd:**
The KOA Holiday in Fountain is running Halloween-themed weekends all month, including October 16–18. You don't have to be a camper — many activities are open to day visitors.

**For members:**
YMCA of the Pikes Peak Region typically runs drop-in programming during school breaks. Check with your location for hours and specific fall break offerings.

D11 parents — your break doesn't start until October 19th, but we'll have that week's guide closer to the date.

What are you planning for break week? Drop your suggestions below — the more ideas the better!

stories.title: Sweet Cubby Loungewear Recall — Flammable Burn Risk

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Did you buy kids' loungewear from Shein? Check the label. Sweet Cubby 2-piece sets (sizes 5-6Y to 13-14Y, batch 272779) are recalled — they fail flammability standards. Email SweetCubby@163.com for a full refund. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting
x_posts.tweet_type: National Parenting — Product Safety / CPSC Recall

facebook.long_form:
If you've shopped Shein for kids' loungewear, this is one to check.

The CPSC recalled approximately 12,461 Sweet Cubby children's loungewear sets on September 11th. The two-piece sets — a short-sleeved shirt with matching shorts — were sold on Shein.com from June 2025 through May 2026 for $8 to $12. They fail the federal flammability standard for children's sleepwear, which means they pose a burn risk.

The recalled sets are in sizes 5-6Y through 13-14Y. Check the neck and seam labels for batch number 272779 — that's the identifier for the recalled product.

What to do: stop using the sets and keep them away from your kids. Email SweetCubby@163.com to request a full refund. You'll need to cut the sets in half and send a photo of the destroyed product before they process it.

No injuries have been reported, but the sizing range covers a lot of families. If you're not sure whether you have this product, it's worth digging through the kids' drawer.

Have you run into any Shein clothing recalls before? This is one where the price point makes the risk easy to miss.

D49 break starts tomorrow, and the good news is there's a lot going on around Colorado Springs this week.

Here's what's worth putting on the calendar for October 12–18:

**Cool Science Festival** runs through October 18th at venues around COS — look for locations on the festival website. Most activities are free, which makes it the easiest yes of the week.

**Boo at the Zoo** at Cheyenne Mountain Zoo is running every October weekend through the end of the month. Tickets are required, so don't wait — weekend slots fill up fast with break week crowd.

**KOA Holiday COS (Fountain)** has Halloween weekends all month. October 16–18 is their "Boo-tastic Science Spree" theme, with trick-or-treating around the campgrounds, campsite decorating, and activities for younger kids. Day visitors are welcome for many activities.

**Garden of the Gods** is always free. Mid-October is peak foliage season in the Front Range, and the park is genuinely stunning this time of year with younger kids who haven't done it yet.

Looking ahead: Pumpkins in the Park (Bancroft Park, free, October 24) and the Garden of the Gods Trunk-or-Treat (October 25) are both coming up soon — keep those on your radar.

stories.title: Halloween Safety Checklist for COS Families

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Two weeks out 🎃 CSPD reminder: plan your route, stick to sidewalks, use glow sticks for dark costumes, and check candy first. Kids are 2x more likely to be hit by a car on Halloween. Stay visible, stay safe. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Two weeks to Halloween, which means it's a good time to run through the checklist before the rush of the last weekend.

Colorado Springs Police and the Red Cross put out similar guidance every year, and honestly the reminders are worth it — kids are more than twice as likely to be hit by a car and killed on Halloween than on any other day of the year. That stat is real and worth sharing.

Here's the checklist we use:

🔦 **Visibility first.** Dark costumes need glow sticks, flashlights, or reflective add-ons. Reflective tape on bags costs almost nothing. Face makeup instead of masks helps kids see around them and cars see them.

🗺️ **Plan the route.** Know where you're going before you leave. Stick to familiar neighborhoods. Set a time to be home if your older kids are going with a group.

🚗 **Watch the streets.** Cross at corners and look both ways — even in a neighborhood with low traffic. Drivers in Colorado have been urged to slow down through residential areas on Halloween night.

🚫 **Never go inside.** Candy comes from the door. That's the rule, even if someone invites them in.

🍬 **Inspect candy before eating.** Anything unwrapped or homemade goes in the trash, full stop.
